__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus that scrapes /api/v1/public/metrics on your ProxCenter.

description: Which Proxmox guests are actually protected, how stale their backups are, and whether the Proxmox Backup Server datastores behind them have room left. Counts guests that have NEVER been backed up, which a dashboard built on backup age alone cannot see. Requires ProxCenter Enterprise with the API option.

panels.title: Protected guests
panels.description: Share of guests holding at least one backup. Guests with none are counted here, which is what proxcenter_backup_protected exists for: an age series alone cannot see them.

panels.title: Guests with no backup
panels.description: Never backed up once. These are invisible to any dashboard built on backup age alone.

panels.title: Guests past the threshold
panels.description: Backed up at some point, but not within the staleness threshold selected above.

panels.title: Oldest backup
panels.description: Neutral on purpose: with nothing backed up there is no age to report, and colouring that green would read as good news.

panels.title: Coverage over the window
panels.description: Average coverage across the selected window rather than at this instant, which is what a compliance report is actually claiming when it quotes a percentage. The outer avg() is not decoration: avg_over_time is a window function applied per series, so without it this tile renders one number per guest.

panels.title: Guests past each staleness bucket
panels.description: Fixed buckets rather than the selected threshold, so the trend stays comparable when someone changes the threshold above. All four series are guest counts, so they share one axis.

defaults.noValue: Every guest has at least one backup
No guest is past the threshold

panels.title: Backups that stopped running

defaults.noValue: Every protected guest was backed up during this window

panels.description: A backup age that grows one second per second means no backup ran during the window. This catches a job that silently stopped, which a staleness threshold only reveals once the threshold is finally crossed.

panels.title: Datastore usage
panels.description: Served pre-computed by ProxCenter, so a datastore whose backend reports no capacity, such as one backed by S3, still charts instead of dividing by zero.

panels.title: Datastore space in use
panels.description: The slope here is what tells you when a datastore runs out, which a usage percentage alone never does.

panels.title: Datastore capacity
panels.description: A capacity and an available figure of 0 mean the backend does not report them, which is normal for an S3-backed datastore. The space in use is still real.

panels.title: Snapshots per datastore
panels.description: A count that stops growing is a backup job that stopped running. A count that falls is pruning.

panels.title: Backup sources by kind

defaults.noValue: No backup source in this selection

panels.description: Distinct sources, by kind: vm, ct and host.

panels.title: Time before a datastore is full
panels.description: At the current trend. The bar is capped at 90 days so that a datastore with days left reads as a short red bar rather than as an invisible sliver next to one with years left. A datastore that is not growing is absent rather than shown as infinite. Needs several hours of history, so read it as a direction and not as a date.

panels.title: Space in use in seven days
panels.description: Projected from the current trend, to read against the capacity in the table above.

panels.title: Backups added per day
panels.description: Snapshots added over a rolling 24 hours. A line falling to zero is a backup job that stopped, which the snapshot count itself never shows because it simply stays high.

panels.title: PBS availability over the window

defaults.noValue: No PBS server in this selection

panels.description: Share of the selected window during which PBS answered, for the WORST server in the selection, which is the figure a compliance claim rests on. A gap here is a window in which no backup could have been taken or verified.

panels.title: PBS reachability
panels.description: A gap in this timeline is a window in which no backup could have been taken or verified.

panels.title: PBS servers

defaults.noValue: No PBS server reporting a version

panels.description: A server whose version is unknown is omitted rather than shown blank, which on this panel means it was unreachable when ProxCenter last read it.

list.name: connection
list.label: PVE connection
list.description: The PVE connection a guest belongs to. This is NOT the PBS server name.

list.name: pbs
list.label: PBS server
list.description: The PBS server. A separate label space from the PVE connection above.

list.name: datastore
list.label: Datastore
list.description: Datastores of the selected PBS servers.

list.name: stale_hours
list.label: Staleness threshold (hours)
list.description: How old a backup has to be before this dashboard calls a guest stale.
